author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The risk of a conflict over Taiwan is shaping Japanese defence planning, with Tokyo shoring up security at home and abroad for a potentially prolonged fight. But there are economic, demographic and political constraints on how far its military transformation can go. In the second of a three-part series, Gabriel Dominguez examines how Tokyo is building military resilience within its territory.
Japan’s recent purchase of a former Nippon Steel site to build a sprawling new defence hub points to a...
title: How Japan is digging in to deter – and withstand – a conflict over Taiwan

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Nicaragua has granted a Chinese-owned company linked to one sanctioned by Washington the right to prospect and dig for gold across 262 sq km (101 sq miles) of rainforest, about a quarter the size of Hong Kong.
The 25-year concession over the block, named Jade, went to Linze Excelente Mineria, a company that appeared in Nicaragua’s mining registry only last year. The block is in a corner of the country where prospectors first struck gold in 1880.
Corporate filings list Lijun Dong as legal...
title: Nicaragua hands gold concession to sister firm of US-sanctioned Chinese miner

author: Wenran Jiang
description:
When US President Donald Trump announced on August 28 that the United States had secured majority control over some 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil through a private company, the North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), he called it “the biggest oil deal in history”.
The White House fact sheet provided the details: NABEP’s 100-year concessions on 17 oilfields with 65 billion barrels of proven reserves, a 35 per cent Pentagon stake, a 20 per cent State Department offtake at cost with...
title: Trump’s Venezuela oil deal: why China can wait and watch

author: Reuters
description:
⁠The US government on Tuesday accused Chinese artificial intelligence companies of maliciously copying technology from American AI firms, potentially complicating relations ahead of a planned meeting between leaders of the world’s two biggest economies later this month.
The Chinese companies ‌copied US AI labs’ intellectual property through a technique known as distillation, according to a statement from US law enforcement and intelligence officials.
Distillation is the process of training...
title: US accuses Chinese AI firms of ‘malicious’ copying of AI technology

author: Igor Patrick
description:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Colombia on Tuesday to meet President Abelardo de la Espriella, sign agreements on critical minerals and civil nuclear cooperation and take up the country’s ties to China, in the first visit by a cabinet-level US official since the Colombian leader took office a month ago.
Colombia’s participation in the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and Chinese investment in critical infrastructure were on the agenda for the meeting, a Colombian official...
title: US Secretary of State Rubio arrives in Colombia to clarify China ties, sign minerals deal

author: Vincent Chow
description:
Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies went on trial on Tuesday in Brooklyn, New York, on criminal charges after eight years of legal wrangling with the US government.
The Shenzhen-based company has pleaded not guilty to all 14 counts, including bank fraud, wire fraud, trade secret theft, and racketeering, with the alleged criminal activity dating back to 1999.
Jury selection began on Tuesday, local time, with US District Judge Ann M. Donnelly of the Eastern District of New York instructing...
title: Huawei goes on trial in US for racketeering after nearly decade of litigation

author: Dewey Sim
description:
President Xi Jinping on Tuesday called for deeper cooperation between “major technological powers” China and the UK as he held his first official call with Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
Xi congratulated Burnham on his appointment as prime minister, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua, emphasising that the shared interests of China and the United Kingdom outweighed their differences in social systems.
“Both sides should respect and trust each other, transcend differences, seek common...
title: China’s Xi Jinping urges deeper UK ties in first call with Andy Burnham

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Pakistan has unveiled a newly acquired Chinese-made short-range air defence system that analysts say could boost its ability to counter Indian drones and low-altitude threats in a future conflict.
A social media video posted by the Pakistan Air Force (PAF) on Sunday confirmed for the first time that it was operating the HQ-17AE short-range air defence (Shorad) system.
The HQ-17AE is an export version of China’s HQ-17A air defence system – a wheeled variant of the original HQ-17 that was...
title: China’s HQ-17AE Shorad system to boost Pakistani drone defence as India tensions simmer

author: Chao Kong
description:
For decades, the United States has used economic and financial restrictions as major foreign policy tools.
But as China and other countries gain greater economic and technological strength, they are also acquiring more ways to push back against US actions, with deep-sea mining possibly becoming a testing ground for that shift.
China could join other countries in taking coordinated countermeasures, including sanctions against companies, if the US proceeds with seabed mining in violation of...
title: Could China sanction US for illegal international seabed mining? A study says yes

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
Qatar on Tuesday vowed to prioritise China’s energy supply and safeguard shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, as both countries coordinated efforts to de-escalate Middle East tensions.
During a meeting in Beijing, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani stressed the importance of unimpeded maritime traffic through the waterway.
Sheikh Mohammed affirmed Doha’s “support for all diplomatic efforts and endeavours...
title: Qatar’s PM vows to prioritise China’s energy supply amid Middle East tensions

author: Denis Simon
description:
When President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for his planned September 24 visit – his first state-level visit to Washington in more than a decade – artificial intelligence is expected to be near the top of the agenda. Both administrations are preparing for their first formal dialogue on AI.
Washington has framed much of that conversation around the need for tighter controls on sensitive technologies. That framing is the problem.
For much of the debate over US science and technology policy...
title: Openness must not be sacrificed in US science and tech policy on China

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s opposition and tour operators have hit back at new registration rules for travellers heading to mainland China, with politicians accusing the ruling Democratic Progressive Party of trying to fan cross-strait fears ahead of local elections.
Since September 1, travellers to the mainland, Hong Kong and Macau have been required to register details of their trip, including the purpose of their visit, contact information, travel dates as well as the numbers of their passports and mainland...
title: Tour industry protests over Taiwan’s new mainland China travel registration rules

author: Meredith Chen
description:
China’s top court has issued new guidance on how judges should handle civil cases involving artificial intelligence, setting out rules on liability for deepfakes, voice cloning, hallucinations and violations of personal rights.
Although Beijing has yet to pass a dedicated AI law, the guidelines expand the country’s legal framework governing the technology.
The Supreme People’s Court’s 24-article opinion, released on Monday, instead provides guidance for handling AI-related disputes under...
title: China’s highest court sets out new AI red lines with rules on deepfakes and privacy

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The United States is stepping up its presence in the South Pacific with new funding and a reinforced diplomatic footprint, as its competition with China intensifies across the region.
Yet the effectiveness of the push is tempered by Washington’s deep cuts to its main overseas aid agency, leaving doubts about the consistency of US commitment among Pacific leaders, according to analysts.
The Pacific island nations are unlikely to frame their foreign relations as a simple choice between the two....
title: US port pledge ups China rivalry in Pacific but island nations stick to own course
Inside Japan’s military build-up

author: Winston Mok
description:
Although President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a brief exchange last week at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, the real action will unfold later this week at the Brics summit when Xi arrives in New Delhi with an expected delegation of 400 officials.
China is one of India’s top trading partners, yet it remains unclear whether Chinese companies are welcome as investors in India. The two countries’ trade and investment relationship...
title: To match China’s economy, India must accept its investment

author: William Zheng
description:
China’s top police officer has pledged deeper cooperation with his Central Asian counterparts to crack down on terrorism, separatism and extremism, while strengthening measures to protect Belt and Road Initiative investments.
Presiding over an informal meeting of the China-Central Asia Public Security and Interior Ministers’ mechanism in Beijing, Chinese Public Security Minister Wang Xiaohong on Monday urged his counterparts from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan to...
title: China rallies Central Asian police chiefs on terrorism threats, energy and trade

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Chinese scientists have proposed developing “underground agriculture” in abandoned coal mine tunnels as part of a push to create a green, circular economy for the country’s massive mining industry.
A team of researchers from Shanxi, a major coal-producing province in central China, described the idea late last month in the journal China Mining Magazine.
An estimated 15,000 abandoned mines in China are expected to close by 2030. Insulated from surface weather and natural disasters, these...
title: Chinese scientists propose turning abandoned coal mines into underground farms

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Fresh off a joint air drill, China will for the first time showcase several PLA Air Force aircraft overseas at an air show this week.
The featured aircraft were selected for the air show in Egypt to demonstrate the air force’s integrated combat abilities and export potential, according to a military analyst.
China’s armed forces on Tuesday posted pictures of Z-20, J-16, YY-20, and KJ-500 with its social media postings about the El Alamein International Airshow. The PLA Air Force said the...
title: Chinese PLA aircraft to headline Egypt air show in display of export potential

author: Liu Zhen
description:
“I do not want to stop [searching]. If I pause, I start thinking about my brothers and sisters and all the moments of my life here.”
Gui Xinwei, deputy chief of the Gyirong Border Inspection Station, was speaking to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV from the ruins of his workplace, seven days after the devastating mudslide erased the port crossing where China and Nepal meet.
“I just don’t want to stop.”
Gui was away on holiday on August 26 when a glacier collapsed in Nepal, triggering a massive...
title: In Gyirong Port, small items speak of the human cost of the China-Nepal disaster

author: Meredith Chen
description:
Calls to reduce English’s status as a core subject in China’s education system have resurfaced after an internet-famous maths teacher urged the country to end “worshipping foreign things”.
The controversy has revived a long-running debate over the role of English in Chinese schools.
The argument came to life again after Tang Jiafeng, a maths teacher known for coaching students through the national postgraduate entrance exam, said on social media that children, parents and schools had devoted...
title: Should Chinese schools demote English as a core subject? Discuss
